# TCH skills

**This is the source.** `.claude/skills/` is a **symlink mirror**, generated by `pnpm skills:sync`.

## Why two folders

The source lives in `.agents/skills/` because it is **neutral** — not tied to any one tool. `.claude/`
exists because Claude Code only looks there.

The mirror must be **symlinks, not copies**. A copy is two truths, and the second one
drifts silently: it keeps working on exactly the machine that broke it, so only a gate
sees it. → `pnpm skills:check`, part of `pnpm build:check`.

## Adding a skill

1. `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — `name` and `description` in the YAML frontmatter, the body is the
   procedure. The name is **kebab-case**, short, action-based (`run-dev`, `tch-dev`).
2. Add `<name>` to [`public-skills.txt`](public-skills.txt) if it belongs to the repo.
3. `pnpm skills:sync`
4. `pnpm skills:check`

## Whitelist

`public-skills.txt` decides which skills git tracks. Every other folder here belongs to one
machine — a skill being tried, a private skill — and is excluded by an **auto-generated** `.gitignore`. That way
playing with skills inside the repo carries no risk of committing them by mistake.

Both `.gitignore` files (`.agents/skills/` and `.claude/skills/`) are written by `skills:sync`. Don't edit them
by hand: the next sync overwrites them.

## Current skills

| Skill | Use when |
|---|---|
| [`run-dev`](run-dev/SKILL.md) | Running TCH locally — web profile, desktop profile, Electron app, private registry |
| [`tch-dev`](tch-dev/SKILL.md) | Fixing and debugging on a **running** surface, borrowing another session's processes instead of killing them |
| [`pr-merge`](pr-merge/SKILL.md) | Taking a change into `main` and out to customers — gates before the PR, description template, journal, and the deploy that comes with the merge |
| [`staging-check`](staging-check/SKILL.md) | Staging acceptance before the PR into `main`: real E2E `--env staging` + a human tester working by hand in a shared window, results into a dated checklist |
